title: Brush Up: The 5-Minute Daily News - AI/Tech, Biz, World
description: Your definitive morning intelligence download. Every day shortly after 7:00 AM EST, we bypass the noise to deliver the critical shifts in AI, Global Business, and Macroeconomics that define the modern landscape. Brush up on the news while you brush up your smile.
latestSummary:
OpenAI renamed its Sora feature from “Cameo” to “Characters” following a court order, reflecting growing IP concerns in AI. The European Parliament banned AI tools on government devices due to security risks and data sovereignty issues. Apple is developing three AI-powered wearables, signaling a broader integration of AI into consumer electronics. India announced a $200 billion AI infrastructure investment plan to become a global AI force.

In markets, stock futures are rising, driven by Nvidia’s deal with Meta, and the UK anticipates a March interest rate cut due to falling inflation. Warren Buffett’s company invested in The New York Times, and Eric Schmidt raised concerns about AI’s electricity demands, proposing space-based data centers.

Geopolitically, peace talks between Russia and Ukraine remain stalled, Peru experienced another presidential change, and Iran reached “guiding principles” with the United States in nuclear talks. The U.S. mourned the death of Jesse Jackson, and rescuers searched for missing skiers in California following an avalanche.

title: Overnight Market Brief - Bridging the Global Gap. Daily.
description:
While North America sleeps, the global economy keeps moving. Overnight Market Brief is your essential pre-market digest, designed for traders, serious investors, and professionals who need to hit the ground running.
Most North American investors miss 50% of the market story because it happens in Tokyo, Hong Kong, and London. We bridge that gap. Every morning at 8:00 AM ET, we deliver a concise, data-driven breakdown and full global picture in under 10 minutes, just in time for your morning commute.
latestSummary:
The Overnight Market Brief – Pre-Market Edition, dated February 18, 2026, provides a market overview following overnight activity in Asia and Europe. Wall Street closed mixed with the S&P 500 up 0.10% and the Nasdaq 100 down 0.13%. Key macro factors include a 10-Year Treasury yield at 4.063%, a Dollar Index at 97.13, and significant gains in Crude Oil (63.97) and Gold (4964.76), suggesting potential inflation concerns.

Asian markets showed mixed performance; Tokyo’s Nikkei 225 rose 1.02% due to strong export data, while Chinese indices experienced divergence due to outdated data. European markets reacted positively to decelerating inflation figures, offering a moderate lead for the US open.

US futures are currently up, with S&P 500 futures rising 0.33% and Nasdaq 100 futures increasing 0.44%. Investors are anticipating the release of Federal Reserve minutes and Japan’s robust export growth as key catalysts. The market appears to favor a continued upward trend, contingent on the Fed’s guidance.

title: Post-market Recap
description:
Did the market "rally into the close" or "fade the open"? The Post-Market Recap goes beyond the green and red arrows to analyze the structure of the trading day. This daily briefing dissects the inter-market correlations that drove the session.
Every afternoon, we cover:
Macro Causality: Connecting the dots between the 10-Year Yield, the Dollar Index, and Equities.
Tech & AI Pulse: A dedicated segment on the semiconductor ecosystem and Big Tech performance.
Market Breadth: Analyzing Volatility (VIX) and Sector Rotation to gauge genuine institutional sentiment.
Closing Catalysts: Identifying the specific news and data that triggered late-day reversals.
latestSummary:
The Post-Market Recap by AGI Era presented the US market’s performance on February 17, 2026, showing a mixed session. The S&P 500 rose 0.10% to 6843.22, while the Nasdaq 100 dipped 0.13% to 24701.60 and the Dow Jones gained 0.07% to 49533.19. Trading volume was elevated, indicating significant participation in the market’s movements.

Investor sentiment was cautiously optimistic, with the market exhibiting resilience despite crosscurrents. Sector performance was divergent, with Technology (XLK) and Utilities (XLU) both declining, suggesting a lack of decisive shifts in risk appetite. The US Dollar Index strengthened, putting upward pressure on 10-year Treasury yields, which negatively impacted interest-rate sensitive sectors. Crude oil prices fell sharply, reflecting concerns about global demand and supply.

Within the “Magnificent Seven,” Nvidia continued its upward trend, while Microsoft, Apple, and Amazon saw gains. Conversely, Microsoft, Google (Alphabet), and Tesla experienced declines, reflecting a shift towards more selective investment strategies. The market appeared to be moving beyond a broad tech rally, focusing on individual company fundamentals.

Looking ahead, investors will be monitoring the dollar’s strength, oil prices, and upcoming economic data. The 6800 level on the S&P 500 remains a key support, and the 10-year yield’s movement will be closely watched for its impact on various sectors.

title: Geopolitical Updates
description: Beyond the headlines lies strategy. Geopolitical Updates is your daily guide to the evolving global order. Each episode provides a rapid scan of the day's top international stories, followed by a deep-dive analysis of the single most impactful event shifting the geopolitical landscape. From tension in the South China Sea to economic statecraft in Europe, we explain not just what happened today, but why it matters for tomorrow. Delivered daily at 7 PM ET.
latestSummary:
The Russia-Ukraine conflict saw initial de-escalation talks in Geneva yielding little progress, highlighting the deep divisions between Kyiv and Moscow. Despite skepticism, the talks represent a crucial diplomatic channel, driven by pressure from the EU and UN to mitigate the conflict’s economic impact. Simultaneously, the U.S. deployed troops to Nigeria to counter Islamist militants, signaling a broader international commitment to counter-terrorism. A detained Russian tanker was released following a fine, demonstrating continued sanctions enforcement efforts.

China’s economic pressure on Japan over Taiwan further complicated the Indo-Pacific landscape. U.S. military operations resulted in eleven fatalities during interdiction efforts against alleged drug trafficking vessels. These developments underscore the ongoing instability and multifaceted nature of global geopolitical tensions. The tentative peace talks in Geneva, despite their initial limitations, remain a critical point of observation for potential shifts in the conflict’s trajectory and broader international implications.
